headline: Congressional Report Urges US to Study Ottoman Relay Inns After Gulf Caravan Raids Stretch Into Third Week
deck: Ancient hospitality meets modern diplomatic ineptitude as Congress suggests turning divorce motels into empire-sized rest stops.
article:
The House Oversight Committee has recommended that the United States adopt 13th-century Ottoman relay stations as a template for handling the Gulf caravan raids now in their third week. These hereditary waystations, which bill guests by lunar cycles, are pitched as the fix for congressional memos that currently require four motel transfers plus a camel quarantine.

Committee Chair Greg Millerson (R-Delaware), who also leads the Association for Misinformation Disclosures, noted that recent strikes have evolved into local festivals featuring bacon-wrapped nuggets and cooling lattes. The bipartisan measure, 'Let Us Chill in Style: Federal Subsidies for Empire-Scale Rest Stops,' calls for rest areas built on 1453 Bursa ledgers that blend leisure with logistics while keeping caffeine flowing. Millerson added that history offers lessons when the prize is a room stocked with expired mustard packets.

Analysts caution the approach could prolong negotiations for months, with funding now linked to camel delivery performance. Borders once patrolled by caravan have become the set for 'America: Caravan Wars,' leaving residents waiting to see what the next convoy delivers.
author: Clara F. Treadwell, Senior Correspondent for Transportation and Cultural Time-Wasting

oped.title: Ottoman Relay Nonsense: My Dynasty Motels Already Solved Everything
oped.author: Horace P. Windbag IV, PhD in Vehicular Nostalgia & Proprietor of the Eternal Slumber Dynasty
oped.body: Congress's push to study Ottoman relay inns during the Gulf caravan raids reveals little confidence in domestic know-how. As proprietor of the Eternal Slumber Dynasty Motel—the sole respectable halt between the Mississippi and the Rockies—I trace the raids to travelers' oversized hats, which provoke raiders like capes before bulls. My fix requires every caravan to pause at my sites for three-week hospitality seminars. This ends the clashes, pads my ledgers, and ruins my ex-wife's rival chain near Tulsa. No need to dust off foreign relics when my properties already convert every journey into a lucrative eternity. The report amounts to another Capitol jab at operators like me.

classifieds.text: Gulf caravan outfit seeks relay-inn keepers fluent in Ottoman guest rites and able to stretch three-week sieges into profitable dynasties; divorce-motel experience mandatory, congressional immunity preferred.

Proud third-generation divorce motel on Route 66, 52 units with built-in alimony lounges, now surplus after Congress ordered Ottoman conversion; will trade for one working camel and a stack of Gulf raid insurance.
Separated trucker, 41, stuck in week-three caravan limbo outside Mobile, seeks fellow refugee fluent in relay etiquette and willing to split the last clean sheets at the next dynasty motel.
Congressional staffer regrets floating the phrase 'empire-sized rest stops' in yesterday's report; all divorce-motel owners are reminded that their alimony archives are not yet nationalized.

panels.caption: Senator waves report: 'Three weeks of Gulf caravan raids! Solution: copy Ottoman relay inns.'
Bureaucrat nods: 'We'll repurpose the divorce motels into horse-swap empires across the continent.'
Driver: 'So my Houston-to-Denver trip now requires swapping saddles every twenty miles? Congress saves the day.'

stories.headline: Divorce Motel Operators Form Coalition to Oppose Ottoman-Style Relay Conversions
stories.deck: Representatives argue that weekly marital dissolution rates would plummet without dedicated suite turnovers.
stories.article:
The National Association of Extended Stay Properties warned that converting properties into relay inns would cut revenue at motels along two-lane routes, where three-day bookings for separating couples make up 87 percent of yearly income.

Lobbyists showed county records indicating that government caravan stops would force chains to slash nightly rates by two-thirds and scrap the express laundry service used for evidence from disputed estates.

stories.headline: Minor League Baseball Teams Add Extra Off Days for Cross-State Bus Caravans
stories.deck: Schedules now list mandatory stops at diner dynasties between single-A away games.
stories.article:
The Midwest League issued its 2026 calendar with built-in four-day travel windows after teams reported that routes between Iowa and Indiana consumed full weeks and wore out pitching staffs.

Officials pointed to last season's data showing 62 percent of road games lost after multi-night motel stays where players roomed with livestock haulers and local insurance agents.
